{{Quote|Don't try to frighten us with your sorcerer's ways, Lord Vader. Your sad devotion to that ancient religion has not helped you conjure up the stolen data-tapes, or given you clairvoyance enough to find the Rebels' hidden fort&mdash;|[[Conan Antonio Motti/Legends|Conan Antonio Motti]]|<ref name="Episode 4">{{Film|IV}}</ref>}}
[[File:DarkForcesDatatape.png|thumb]]
A '''data-tape''', also '''information tape''', was a recording device that could be read by a [[Holoprojector/Legends|holoprojector]], such as the one standard in [[R2-series astromech droid/Legends|R2 units]], or a [[computer terminal]].

==History==
The [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] training ship ''[[Chu'unthor]]'' had many datatapes about [[Jedi training/Legends|Jedi training]]. When it crashed in [[340 BBY]], [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] led a rescue team to the wreck. He left the datatapes and reader discs about the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], and prophesied a Jedi to defeat the [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsisters]]. In [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]], [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] fulfilled the prophecy and took the records. In [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], these were the majority in the collection of Jedi datatapes of the [[New Jedi Order]].<ref name="TEGTTF">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref>

The [[Death Star plans/Legends|plans]] for the first [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] were recorded on datatapes, which were stolen by a rebel force and provided to [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] and uploaded into [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]]. Later, the tapes came into the possession of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Rebellion]], and helped in the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]].

==Behind the scenes==
The use of the word "tapes" in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']] was in [[1977]]. In the 1970s, tapes were a modern way of recording audio, video, and computer data.
